bullets.title: Iran deal imminent or stalled? Conflicting signals keep markets on edge
bullets.body: Trump declared the US-Iran deal 'scheduled to be signed Sunday,' cited 100M+ barrels transiting Hormuz, and said no money would change hands. But Iran's foreign ministry denied a final nuclear MOU, said negotiating teams weren't heading to Geneva, and its parliament proposed a bill to charge for Hormuz transit. Pakistani PM confirmed a framework has been reached; Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Turkey are active mediators. Wolfe Research notes an actual MOU looks distant—the key unlock remains Treasury yields above 4.5% forcing Trump's hand. CENTCOM confirmed a 3rd round of strikes on Iran as of mid-week.

bullets.title: ECB hikes 25bps, signals further tightening possible; BoJ expected to follow
bullets.body: The ECB raised all key rates 25bps to 2.25% in a unanimous decision—first hike since 2023—cutting 2026 growth to 0.8% and raising inflation to 3.0% for 2026. Lagarde said no pre-set rate path, but sources flagged July as live. JPMorgan expects one more hike in September. The Bank of Japan is expected to hike to 1.00% next week; BOJ Governor Ueda was hospitalized but officials said it won't disrupt policy. Bank of Canada held at 2.25%.

bullets.title: Fed hawkish pivot: no 2026 cuts likely; 2-4 hikes possible in late 2026/2027
bullets.body: Multiple research desks align: June FOMC will remove the easing bias, June dot plot likely shows 0 cuts in 2026 with median 2026 dot shifting up 25bps. Core PCE tracking 33-38bps for May (up from 21-26bps prior), driven by PPI upside in portfolio management fees and airfares. Futures market is pricing one hike by year-end. Key debate is whether Chair Warsh focuses on trimmed mean PCE vs. core PCE. 22V and GS both see 2-4 hike sequence as increasingly plausible in late 2026/2027.

bullets.title: May CPI 4.2% YoY as expected; core 0.2% MoM misses (good); PPI a shock
bullets.body: May CPI printed +0.47% MoM / +4.2% YoY in line with consensus; core came in at +0.21% (consensus 0.3%)—largely driven by car insurance reversing. However, May PPI was a shock: headline +1.1% vs 0.7% est, with final demand goods the largest monthly jump on record (+2.8%). Core PCE is now tracking ~0.35-0.38% MoM, pushing 12-month core PCE toward 3.4-3.5%. JPMorgan calls May 'high-water mark' for CPI but markets remain hawkish.

bullets.title: Tech selloff deepens—semis/AI capex stocks under pressure all week
bullets.body: The week saw a major tech unwind: SOX fell sharply then recovered; XLK down ~12% from highs at the lows. ORACLE -8-11% on earnings (strong bookings but $40B financing plan alarmed; gross margin set to compress). ADBE -7-9% on CEO/CFO departures and organic ARR guide-down. SMCI -25-28% on $7B equity raise. Key debate: is 'CPO delay' thesis (SemiAnalysis) or 'no delay' thesis (FundaAI/Lumentum CEO) correct? NVIDIA affirmed CPO on track, 800V no delay. Retail sold semis at record pace.

bullets.title: AI capex concerns: Oracle $70B net capex, hyperscaler spreads drift from AA to A
bullets.body: Oracle guided $90-95B gross capex for FY27 ($70B net after $20-25B customer prepayments), raising ~$40B in debt/equity. Hyperscaler IG leverage doubled to 1.8x in 6 months; Morgan Stanley projects $570B in AI-related debt issuance in 2026—nearly 2x FY25. GS notes consensus $920B FY27 capex estimate too conservative; likely $1.1-1.4T. AMZN issued record Canadian bond deal; GOOGL issued record JPY bond deal. Credit spreads drifting from AA to A territory.

bullets.title: SpaceX IPO dominates sentiment: 4x oversubscribed, $1.75T valuation, $75B raise
bullets.body: SpaceX IPO priced at $135, opened ~$165 (trading ~30-35% first-day pop), raising $75B in the largest IPO in history. Retail allocated at least 20%, Middle East sovereign funds placed $1-5B orders each, ARK bought $444M on day 1. SPCX began trading on Nasdaq. 2x leveraged long ($SPCH) and short ($SSPC) ETFs launched Monday. Cramer compared to Cerebras but more moderate. Wolfe initiated at Outperform $175 PT on Starship reusability thesis.

bullets.title: OpenAI filing confidentially for IPO; Anthropic $35B financing deal closed
bullets.body: OpenAI confidentially filed for IPO targeting $1T valuation and expects to go public within a year per Altman. Anthropic closed a $35B financing round (AVGO-led XPV platform with Apollo/Blackstone). OpenAI is considering drastic token price cuts to compete with Anthropic and fight customer pushback on AI costs. Token prices fell 6 days in a row—longest streak since January. Anthropic also began leasing first data centers, with GOOGL providing financial guarantees.

bullets.title: AI model governance: US government forced Anthropic to block Fable/Mythos foreign access
bullets.body: Amazon CEO Jassy's talks with Trump administration reportedly triggered a sweeping crackdown halting foreign access to Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models per WSJ. Analysts note the US-China AI infrastructure binary: companies must choose either Chinese open models/Huawei stack or US government-dependent models. Export controls at model layer set precedent. Microsoft restricted Claude Fable for employees over data retention concerns. MSFT Xbox planning major layoffs post June 30 fiscal year end.

bullets.title: US equity positioning: near decade lows in concentration; broadening trade gaining
bullets.body: GS Prime: global equities net bought for 4th consecutive week, 4.7:1 short cover to long sale ratio. Info Tech net sold at fastest 2-month pace led by short sales. HF net leverage fell to 8th percentile. MS equity strategists note S&P ex-AI (SPXXAI) and Cyclicals (GSXUCYCL) as preferred broadening trade implementation. Equal-weight S&P outperformed cap-weight by ~120bps. Russell 2000 up 2x SPY YTD (+19% vs +17.4% NDX). Tech now >51% of S&P 500.

bullets.title: Software sector collapse: ADBE -19%, ORCL -14% weekly; IGV down 9 sessions
bullets.body: UBS flags ADBE as pivoting to freemium model—deflationary for software economics; similar moves at TEAM, MSFT, NOW. ORCL cloud revenue missed at $9.91B vs $10B expected. IGV fell in 9 consecutive sessions on ORCL/ADBE earnings. Wolfe downgrades ADBE to Peer Perform; fair value $165-210. Token maximization theme reaching crescendo per Karl Keirstead. PLTR named top pick for software rerating.

bullets.title: Memory supercycle: CSPs locking 2028 LTAs; MU FY27 EPS estimates surge to $124-135
bullets.body: Wolfe and JPMorgan both sharply raised MU estimates: FY27 EPS to $124-135 vs Street ~$107-111. HBM pricing expected +40% YoY in CY27. DRAM ASP rising 35% QoQ in CQ2 following 75% in Q1. CSPs have locked all 2027 capacity and are now securing 2028 LTAs. Memory now larger than entire Energy sector in IG leverage. SK Hynix plans to triple wafer capacity by 2034. China's WF6 export controls threatening semiconductor supply (TSMC, Samsung affected).

bullets.title: Optical selloff on CPO delay report—but LITE CEO and NVDA confirm no delay
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis published a report suggesting CPO and 800V DC architecture were pushed out to 2028-2029. This triggered a sharp selloff in LITE, COHR, AAOI, CIEN, GLW. But Lumentum CEO at Mizuho conference confirmed H2 2027 CPO scale-up shipment start with formal ramp in 2028—consistent with prior guidance. NVDA Senior VP confirmed no delay in CPO ramp. JPMorgan views selloff as overblown, reiterates OW on COHR and LITE at sub-1x PEG.

bullets.title: India IT sector selloff continues—AI obsolescence concerns, down ~50% from peak
bullets.body: India's stock market remained in downtrend all year led by IT consulting/outsourcing stocks down ~50%. AI obsolescence is the primary catalyst. IT sector was 25% of Sensex at peak, now 14%. ACN similarly faces risk as enterprises shift from 3P contractors to internal AI tooling. Citi IT Day confirmed enterprises reallocating IT budgets toward AI and reducing 3P contractor spend.

bullets.title: INTC double-upgrade at BofA to Buy $135 PT on foundry momentum and CPU TAM expansion
bullets.body: BofA double-upgraded INTC from Underperform to Buy ($135 PT, +26% upside) citing leading-edge wafer and packaging opportunities. BofA also raised 2030 server CPU TAM forecast 36% to $170B+ on agentic AI demand. GOOGL discussing Samsung for TPU v10 I/O die on 2nm. INTC 18A Cadence co-optimization deal announced. Foundry utilization rates back to 2021 levels but Intel stands out with >90% utilization.

bullets.title: Crude oil down sharply on Iran deal hopes; World Bank cuts 2026 global growth
bullets.body: Brent fell below $90 (down 6-7% on week), WTI settled ~$84-88 range, gold fell 3% to $4,150-4,200/oz. Goldman cut 2027 Brent forecast citing weak demand. OPEC cut 2026 demand growth forecast to 970K bpd. World Bank cut 2026 global GDP to 2.5% from 2.6%. Hyperscaler debt spread drifted from AA to A within IG. SPR at 2-year low. US crude exports at record high +116% over 2 months.

bullets.title: Leveraged ETF structural risk: $15B/1% SPX move, >$230B AUM at >99th percentile
bullets.body: MS QDS report flags levered ETF short gamma at $15B per 1% SPX move (beta-adjusted), still >99th percentile historically. SOXL generated $12B rebalancing demand in a single session—45% of its prior-day AUM—cited as 3rd largest ETF volume day in 20 years. Total leveraged and inverse single-stock ETF AUM hit $300B+ with $750B+ underlying exposure. Two 2x SpaceX ETFs launched week of 6/13. Record $90B flowed through high-risk leveraged ETFs in a single day.

bullets.title: Geopolitical: US-Iran strikes escalate; Israel prepares; Lebanon heating up
bullets.body: CENTCOM confirmed multiple rounds of self-defense strikes on Iranian air defense systems through the week. Iran fired ballistic missiles at US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan. IRGC claimed closure of Strait of Hormuz to all vessels but CENTCOM denied. An Apache helicopter was downed near Hormuz—crew rescued. Israel's military chief signaled readiness to 'return immediately' to fighting. 15 ships/day using Omani channel with US air cover per FT.

bullets.title: Amazon expands LTL freight nationally, pressuring trucking sector
bullets.body: Amazon launched its less-than-truckload freight service to all businesses (previously limited to Amazon facilities), immediately pressuring ODFL (-6%), SAIA (-7%), XPO (-4%), FDXF (-6%). Separately, Amazon secured a $17.5B delayed-draw term loan facility from Citigroup to fund AI capex. Amazon also partnered with OpenAI on AWS inferencing.
